info.title: Falsify
info.description: A backtesting engine that tries to prove your strategy wrong. Local API: cached data, strategies, backtests, saved runs.

get.description: Broker instruments with their contract specification.
What data is cached for this instrument, and how healthy it is.

post.description: Downloads the part of a period the cache does not already hold.

get.description: Where a watched call has got to, polled beside the call itself.

schema.title: Response List Strategies Api Strategies Get

post.description:
Validates a spec and writes it to `strategies/`.

Refuses to replace an existing file unless asked to: the most likely way
to reach this endpoint is "duplicate one of the library strategies and
change it", and silently overwriting the original would be the worst
possible outcome of that flow.
Validates a spec without saving it. The errors are the human-readable ones.

get.description:
What a spec may contain, straight from the registry and the models.

The editor renders whatever is here and nothing else. Duplicating this
list in the frontend is how a spec becomes valid on screen and invalid on
the server.

post.description: What this spec is about to cost, before any backtest is run.
Gate zero: does the signal beat the spread, before even talking SL/TP?
Launches a backtest. If it takes over two seconds the run_id returns immediately.

schema.title: Response List Runs Api Runs Get

get.description:
Equity curve and drawdown, reduced to ~`points` points.

The drawdown is computed on the **whole** series and only then are the
points reduced, otherwise the minimum would be measured on an already
pruned curve.

post.description:
Curves aligned on the same axis and metrics side by side.

The curves are normalized to 100 at the start of their own period: two
runs with different initial equity, or over different periods, stay
comparable.
Optimize in-sample, apply out-of-sample, one window at a time.
The real result against random entries and against permuted price paths.
What the observed Sharpe is worth given how many configurations were tried.
Ambiguous trades settled with tick data, or a plain statement that they cannot be.
The same spec across many instruments, and whether they agree.
Starts a screening campaign and returns the job to poll.

get.description:
Stage zero: which instrument x timeframe pairs are worth testing at all.

The spread comes from each instrument's M1 sample, never from the bars
being judged: above M1 that column is the minimum spread inside the bar,
which on this broker is zero on most FX hours.

Every diary under the live directory, most recent activity first.

The backend does not run the runner: `scripts.run_live` does, in its own
process, with its own lock. This reads what that process wrote, so the
dashboard can be opened and closed without touching a running strategy.

schema.title: Response List Live Sessions Api Live Get

get.description: One runner: its state, its recent diary, and its closed trades.

Expected versus realized: a backtest of exactly the diary's own period.

The backtest is computed here rather than looked up, over the bars the
runner actually saw, so the two records describe the same period by
construction. Comparing against a backtest of a different window would
measure the window.

AmbiguityPriorOut.title: AmbiguityPriorOut
AmbiguityPriorOut.description: A-priori share of trades a bar-resolution backtest cannot settle.

AttemptsPanelOut.title: AttemptsPanelOut
AttemptsPanelOut.description:
The multiple-testing correction at two scopes; see `core.research.preview`.

The unprefixed fields are the local scope - this instrument over an
overlapping period. The `overall_` fields are the whole search, which is
what the campaign report quotes and what governs a claim of discovery.

DownloadRequest.title: DownloadRequest
DownloadRequest.description:
Ask the broker for the part of a period the cache does not hold.

Only the holes are fetched. Asking for a range that is already cached is
a valid request that downloads nothing and says so, which is the honest
answer and also the cheap one.

ProgressOut.title: ProgressOut
ProgressOut.description:
How far into a job the server is.

`total` of zero means the work has no countable steps, and the client is
expected to say that it is running rather than invent a share.

ScreenJobOut.title: ScreenJobOut
ScreenJobOut.description: A campaign takes minutes: it is a job, polled, not a blocked request.

SpreadCoverageOut.title: SpreadCoverageOut
SpreadCoverageOut.description:
How much of a run's period had an M1 sample to measure the spread on.

A run whose `measured_share` is low was charged a constant taken from a
different period. That is not wrong, but it is an assumption, and it is
the assumption most able to move a marginal result.

SpreadRealismOut.title: SpreadRealismOut
SpreadRealismOut.description: What a run's spread policy charged, and whether a fill could have paid it.

VocabularyOut.title: VocabularyOut
VocabularyOut.description:
Everything the strategy editor is allowed to build out of.

Served rather than duplicated in the frontend: a tenth indicator, a new
parameter or a renamed bar field has to reach the editor by appearing
here, and cannot reach it by someone remembering to update a second list.
